values.note: 16 campsites, 2 accessible, in a forested area with trails to the shoreline.

sites.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r01/bitterroot/recreation/schumaker-campground ('It features 16 campsites, with two vault toilets and two accessible sites', 'Maximum vehicle length 55 feet.'; last updated October 19, 2026), read 2026-10-22

values.note: Two vault toilets. Pack it in, pack it out; no garbage service. Motorized boats prohibited on Twin Lakes.

facilities.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r01/bitterroot/recreation/schumaker-campground ('two vault toilets'; 'Potable water is not available at this site.'; 'Pack it in, Pack it out, no garbage service provided.'), read 2026-10-22

values.note: Forest Service: 'Open yearlong until closed by snow.'
At least one person must occupy the site the first night; equipment may not be left unattended more than 24 hours. Dispersed camping along Lost Horse Road if full.

booking.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r01/bitterroot/recreation/schumaker-campground ('Campsites are available on a first come/first served basis.', 'Camping is limited to 16 consecutive days', 'If Schumaker Campground is full, there are opportunities for dispersed camping along Lost Horse Road.'), read 2026-10-22

note: Bitterroot NF (Darby RD), on the edge of Twin Lakes near the Selway-Bitterroot Wilderness and the Twin Lakes Trailhead at ~6,575 ft. Access is ~18 mi up Lost Horse Road (FR 429) from Hwy 93 between Hamilton and Darby, then ~2 mi on FR 5605 at the Lost Horse Guard Station; the Forest Service calls FR 429 'narrow, rough, and fairly steep in some places' and 'extremely rough due to many potholes and rocks', and recommends high clearance. Call Darby Ranger Station for road conditions. --Claude
summary: Forest Service page (updated Oct 19, 2026): confirmed 16 sites (2 accessible), vault toilets, free, FCFS; added 55-ft max vehicle length, no drinking water, 16-day limit, attended-site rule, season 'open yearlong until closed by snow'. Alerts: only a prescribed burn elsewhere (Hughes Creek). Note trimmed of restated values; access caveats kept.
flags: Criteria problem (high clearance): the Forest Service recommends high clearance for the only access, Lost Horse Road FR 429 ('dirt road that is narrow and rough... High clearance vehicles recommended'; 'can be extremely rough due to many potholes and rocks. High clearance vehicles are recommended'), ~18 miles of it. EKKO is not 4WD/high clearance.

Waterfront re-audit lead: entry is 'not waterfront' but the Forest Service page says the campground 'sits on the edge of Twin Lakes' and 'Campsites have trails leading to the shoreline' (https://www.fs.usda.gov/r01/bitterroot/recreation/schumaker-campground). Not changed.
